chains.earliest_control: phishing-resistant MFA required for the highly privileged roles
chains.name: Takeover of a privileged administrator

steps.text: The tenant's domain and its Microsoft 365 sign-in page are public; two of the three privileged users are Global Administrators, so any one of them is a full-tenant target.

An adversary-in-the-middle phishing page relays an administrator's sign-in: MFA is enforced by authentication strength, but not the phishing-resistant strength, for all users or for privileged roles (MS.AAD.3.1v1, MS.AAD.3.6v1). Alternative routes run through the account excluded from the legacy-authentication block (MS.AAD.1.1v1) or the exclusions on the device-code block (MS.AAD.3.9v1); whose accounts those are is UNKNOWN (H6).

None is needed: six highly privileged roles carry permanent active assignments, four are assigned outside PIM, and Global Administrator activation needs no approval (MS.AAD.7.4v1, MS.AAD.7.5v1, MS.AAD.7.6v1); Global Administrator is used where finer-grained roles would do (MS.AAD.7.2v1).

New role assignments go unannounced: six roles send no assignment notification and five send none on activation (MS.AAD.7.7v1, MS.AAD.7.9v1), so an added administrator or application credential can stand unseen.

chains.earliest_control: user consent to applications restricted, with requests routed to the admin consent workflow
chains.name: Illicit consent through a third-party application

steps.text: A user is lured to consent to an attacker's multi-tenant application, which the authorization policy allows even for risky delegated permissions (MS.AAD.5.2v1); any user may also register applications (MS.AAD.5.1v1).
The grant outlives a password reset and sits among the 10 applications and 1 third-party service principal the scan already flags as holding risky permissions (A10).
Mail and files are read through Microsoft Graph as the application, activity that sign-in protections do not cover.

chains.earliest_control: SharePoint external sharing limited to existing guests or to people in the organization
chains.name: Anonymous links into SharePoint content

steps.text: SharePoint external sharing is set to Anyone (MS.SHAREPOINT.1.1v1), so a forwarded or leaked link opens content without sign-in.
Anyone links on folders allow edit, not view only (MS.SHAREPOINT.3.2v1): the holder of a folder link can add or replace files for the 30 days the link lives.
A planted file reaches staff from a trusted site; Safe Attachments does not scan SharePoint, OneDrive or Teams files (MS.SECURITYSUITE.1.4v1).

chains.earliest_control: a DLP policy restricting connector access in the default Power Platform environment
chains.name: Data movement through unrestricted Power Platform connectors

steps.text: Any signed-in user, or an attacker holding one user's session from Chain A or B, can build a flow in the default environment.

With no DLP policy in the default environment (MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.1v1) or the other environment (MS.POWERPLATFORM.2.2v1), the flow can join a business connector to any non-business connector and copy data out; Purview DLP covers Devices only, not SharePoint, OneDrive or Exchange (MS.SECURITYSUITE.3.2v1).
